title: Milwaukee French Immersion School community protests teacher cuts
seoTitle: Milwaukee school community protests teacher cuts

tea.why: Parents, teachers, and students protested against recent staffing cuts and classroom consolidations at their school.
tea.want: They want the district to reinstate the eliminated teacher and reverse the staffing cuts.
tea.changed: Oct 12: School community members staged a demonstration outside the MPS headquarters.

summary: On October 12, parents, teachers, and students from the Milwaukee French Immersion School demonstrated outside the Milwaukee Public Schools headquarters in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Organised by the school's Parent Teacher Association, the protest aimed to voice opposition against staffing reductions and class consolidations. Demonstrators chanted slogans demanding that officials leave teachers alone and revoke the cuts. According to the PTA president, a district-ordered audit prompted hiring, but because enrollment fell slightly short of projections, the district decided to eliminate a teaching position, impacting multiple classrooms. In response, an MPS spokesperson stated that the K4 enrollment fell below sustainable guidelines and that the staffing adjustments bring class sizes to about 20 students while maintaining a supportive adult-to-student ratio. The district also noted that about 55 teachers are being moved from lower-enrollment schools to help fill current vacancies elsewhere.
organizers: Milwaukee French Immersion School Parent Teacher Association
response: An MPS spokesperson stated that the current K4 enrollment was below guidelines and financially unsustainable. The district noted that the adjustment creates two classes of about 20 students each with paraprofessionals, and that about 55 teachers are being shifted to help fill vacancies.
